result.title: RoleFlow: Self-Evolving Multi-Role Agentic Collaboration via Structural Adaptation
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving task requirements. Although recent approaches enable dynamic orchestration, trajectory-level rewards they apply assign one outcome to each decision, ofen struggling to identify the contributions of individual structural changes. We propose RoleFlow, a self-evolving multi-role agentic system that refines collaboration structures through feedback-driven atomic edits and on-demand role synthesis. To make structural adaptation learnable, we introduce Single-Edit Counterfactual Policy Optimization (SECPO), which evaluates each edit against its no-edit counterpart at the same chain state and assigns targeted credit to edit-specific tokens. Across seven benchmarks spanning four domains, RoleFlow achieves the optimal average performance, surpassing the strongest competitor by 4.7 points. It leads on all three multi-hop QA benchmarks by 3.2-7.5 F1 points and also shows supremacy on mathematical reasoning, web interaction, and code generation. Further analyses demonstrate cross-benchmark transferability, training-data efficiency, and cross-executor generalization.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RoleFlow，通过反馈驱动的原子编辑与按需角色合成自适应调整多智能体协作结构，并用 SECPO 在同一链状态下对照「无编辑」版本，为单次结构编辑分配针对性信用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单步反事实对照 + 定向信用」可能可供核查 latent 推理中轨迹级奖励难以归因到具体推理步骤或状态更新这一问题，但对象是多智能体协作拓扑而非视觉 latent 状态，迁移线索仍需人工确认。
